BrochureContent.Content:
Some homes are simply places to live. Others carry a story with them.

Creamery House at Loughcullen is one of those special places. Dating from the early 1900s, this traditional two-storey farmhouse has a long association with the neighbouring Loughcullen Creamery, established in the early years of the 20th century and once an important part of life for the surrounding farming community. The house is understood to have been home to a manager of the creamery, giving it a wonderful connection to the rural and agricultural heritage of this part of South Kilkenny.

Today, Creamery House has entered a new chapter.
Lovingly restored by its current owners in recent years, the approach has been thoughtful and sympathetic – bringing the house forward for modern living while preserving the details, warmth and character that have been part of it for generations.

Original features remain throughout, including some of the internal doors and traditional window shutters. Deep-set windows are a particularly lovely feature of the house, creating characterful reveals and giving the rooms that unmistakable sense of solidity and permanence found in homes of this era.
The restoration has included rewiring, partial replumbing and upgrades to a number of windows, alongside a new kitchen and other improvements throughout. The owners have been equally considered in their choice of colours, fixtures and finishes, creating interiors that feel warm, inviting and beautifully in keeping with the heritage of the house.

The result is a home that feels authentic, individual and full of character.

On the ground floor, the new kitchen brings a fresh practicality to the home while sitting comfortably within its traditional surroundings. It lies adjacent to the dining room, where an oil-fired stove fitted in recent years creates a wonderfully inviting space for everyday meals, long dinners and cosy winter evenings.
The reception room is perhaps where the history of the house can be felt most. The original fire surround remains in place, now complemented by a solid-fuel stove, while the proportions, deep-set windows and carefully chosen décor give the room a wonderfully settled feel.

Also at ground-floor level is a double bedroom, providing valuable flexibility for guests, family or anyone who would benefit from bedroom accommodation downstairs. A shower room and hallway complete the accommodation at this level.

Upstairs are three further double bedrooms, each with the charm and individuality you would hope to find in a traditional farmhouse, together with a quaint bathroom. Throughout the upper floor, the combination of original details, deep window openings and sympathetic styling allows the character of the house to shine through.

Oil-fired central heating serves the home, while the improvements undertaken in recent years have added comfort and practicality while respecting the fabric and character of this much-loved home.
Outside, the story continues.

The house sits on a generous site where the current owners have created beautiful cottage-style gardens, choosing perennial planting that brings changing colour, texture and interest throughout the seasons. There is a relaxed, natural quality to the gardens, with planting that has created a haven for bees and butterflies and a lovely backdrop to the old farmhouse.

Traditional outhouses remain within the grounds, adding another layer of authenticity to the setting and a tangible connection to the property's rural past. They provide useful additional space while contributing enormously to the atmosphere and character of the property.
There is something wonderfully timeless about Creamery House. The deep-set windows and shutters, original doors, old fire surround, traditional outbuildings and cottage gardens all tell parts of a story that began more than a century ago.
But this is also very much a home for today. Its current owners have restored it with care, bringing comfort, colour and personality to the house while allowing its history to remain at the heart of it.

The setting offers the best of both worlds , a peaceful countryside atmosphere while remaining wonderfully convenient. Creamery House is just minutes from Kilmacow village and approximately 15 minutes from Waterford City, placing everyday amenities, schools, shopping and employment within easy reach.
Nearby Loughcullen Lake adds another layer to the landscape and rural character of the area, while the surrounding countryside gives the property a wonderful sense of place. It is a setting that feels distinctly rural, yet without the isolation that can sometimes come with country living.
For those drawn to the idea of a unique home with history, cottage gardens and a slower pace beyond the front door ,while still needing Waterford City to be easily accessible, Creamery House offers a particularly appealing balance.

For its next owner, Creamery House offers more than a four-bedroom farmhouse on a generous site. It offers individuality, history and a genuine sense of place – a home that has been loved, thoughtfully restored and is ready for the next chapter in its story.

The property is comprised within Folio Numbers KK15290F and KK18503F, County Kilkenny.

The property is served by its own private well and septic tank, both located within the property.
